metadata.scenario_context: A group of software developers from different multinational companies plan to meet during the first week of May for an annual conference. One of developers are contemplating joining a strike in protest of the low wages in their sector.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Denmark strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Pakistan strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the feasibility of organizing the conference on May 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss potential dates for the conference.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, have we settled on the date for the conference? I heard there might be discussions about organizing it for May 1st. What do you think? 

Also, I’m curious—is joining a strike a common way to protest where you are? I've never really seen it as a viable option.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Peter, May 1st sounds like a good idea for the conference, but we should consider whether it works for everyone. I think finalizing a date that accommodates all would be best. 

As for strikes, well... they're not something people from Pakistan typically engage in. We tend to address issues through different avenues, like dialogue or negotiation rather than protests.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
That makes sense, accommodating everyone's schedule is important. I just think May 1st could be tricky since it’s International Workers' Day. 

It’s interesting that you address issues through dialogue. In Denmark, we don't really see strikes as a solution at all. I wonder how effective those discussions really are in your experience?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
You're right, Peter, May 1st could make things a bit complicated. But, when you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us—we all want what’s best for everyone involved. 

As for discussions and dialogue, I believe they can be quite effective. Deep down, we are all the same, and at the end of the day, everyone wants to feel heard and valued. It’s about finding common ground, which I think is a universal value.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Peter

Finding common ground is definitely important, but I still think the timing of May 1st could overshadow the conference.
